- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

attachment.content:
- graphify: Use for any question about a codebase, its architecture, file relationships, or project content — especially when graphify-out/ exists, where the question should be treated as a graphify query first. Turns any input (code, docs, papers, images, videos) into a persistent knowledge graph with god nodes, community detection, and query/path/explain tools.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

content.text:
h14.

**Computation site:** `RebuildMemoPayload()` in `server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:74-88`, which calls `markdownService.ExtractAll()` (`internal/markdown/markdown.go:356-422`) to walk the goldmark AST of `memo.Content` in a single pass.

**Triggers (recomputation):**
- `CreateMemo` — always run on new memos: `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:108` (before `s.Store.CreateMemo`).
- `UpdateMemo` — only when the update mask includes the `content` path (i.e., the memo body itself is edited): `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:436-449`.
- A batch maintenance path also exists — `Runner.RunOnce()` in `server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:27-72` rebuilds the payload for *all* memos in paginated batches of 100 and persists via `Store.UpdateMemo`. (Note: this runner isn't currently wired into any startup/cron path in the codebase — only its exported `RebuildMemoPayload` function is invoked, from `memo_service.go`.)

**Extracted properties**, stored on `store.Memo.Payload` (`storepb.MemoPayload`, defined in `proto/store/memo.proto:7-21`):
- `Tags` (`[]string`) — all `#tag` nodes found in content.
- `Property.Title` — text of the first block-level node if it's an H1 heading.
- `Property.HasLink` — set if any Markdown link node exists.
- `Property.HasCode` — set if any code block/fenced code block/code span exists.
- `Property.HasTaskList` — set if any task checkbox exists.
- `Property.HasIncompleteTasks` — set if any task checkbox is unchecked.

(A `Mentions` field is also part of `ExtractedData`, but it's not written into `MemoPayload`; it's used separately in `memo_mention_helpers.go:32-42` via its own `ExtractAll` call to create mention relations, not for list/preview metadata.)

## Summary

This is the **usememos/memos** Go backend (note-taking app). "Memo" objects have derived metadata computed from markdown content, used for previews/lists.

### 1. Model/schema definitions

- **Go store model**: `/bench/home/work/store/memo.go:35-55` — `store.Memo` struct, field `Payload *storepb.MemoPayload` (line 51) holds all derived data.
- **Proto schema (source of truth for derived fields)**: `/bench/home/work/proto/store/memo.proto:7-29`
  ```proto
  message MemoPayload {
    Property property = 1;
    Location location = 2;
    repeated string tags = 3;
    message Property {
      bool has_link = 1;
      bool has_task_list = 2;
      bool has_code = 3;
      bool has_incomplete_tasks = 4;
      string title = 5;  // "extracted from the first H1 heading, if present"
    }
    ...
  }
  ```
  Comment at line 14: "The calculated properties from the memo content."
- Generated Go code: `/bench/home/work/proto/gen/store/memo.pb.go`.
- API-layer proto: `/bench/home/work/proto/api/v1/memo_service.proto` (exposes `snippet`, `tags`, `property` fields on the API `Memo` message).

### 2. Function(s) that compute derived metadata

All in `/bench/home/work/internal/markdown/markdown.go` (goldmark-based `markdown.Service`):
- **`ExtractAll(content []byte) (*ExtractedData, error)`** — lines 356-422. Single-pass walk that extracts `Tags`, `Mentions`, and `Property{Title, HasLink, HasCode, HasTaskList, HasIncompleteTasks}` together (this is the one actually used for memo payload rebuilds — "efficient" single parse).
- `ExtractProperties(content []byte)` — lines 193-241 (same property logic, standalone/unused-by-rebuild variant).
- `GenerateSnippet(content []byte, maxLength int) (string, error)` — lines 264-346: strips markdown to plain text, truncates at word boundary (used for preview snippets, **not stored**, computed on every read).
- `ExtractedData` struct — lines 21-25.

### 3. What triggers recomputation

The rebuild wrapper: `func RebuildMemoPayload(_ context.Context, memo *store.Memo, markdownService markdown.Service) error` at `/bench/home/work/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:74-88`. It calls `markdownService.ExtractAll(...)` and sets `memo.Payload.Tags` / `memo.Payload.Property`.

It is invoked explicitly (no ORM hook/middleware — this is plain Go/sqlx, not an ORM with lifecycle hooks) at:
- **Create**: `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:108` inside `CreateMemo`, before `s.Store.CreateMemo(ctx, create)`.
- **Update**: `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:447` inside `UpdateMemo`, only when the `content` field path is present in the update mask (line 436 `if path == "content"`), before `s.Store.UpdateMemo(ctx, update)`.
- **Batch/maintenance job**: `Runner.RunOnce(ctx)` at `/bench/home/work/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:27-72` rebuilds payloads for all memos in batches of 100 and persists via `Store.UpdateMemo`. **Notably, this runner is not registered anywhere** — `/bench/home/work/server/server.go:153-175` (`startBackgroundRunners`) only wires up `s3presign.NewRunner`; `memopayload.NewRunner`/`RunOnce` has no caller in the codebase (grep confirms zero references outside its own file), so it's effectively dead/manual-only code, not an active cron job.

Separately, **`Snippet` is not stored at all** — it's computed on every read/conversion via `getMemoContentSnippet` (`/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go:83-89`, calling `GenerateSnippet(content, 64)`), invoked from `convertMemoFromStoreWithCreators` at `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go:76-80` and similarly for related-memo snippets (lines 221-273) and notification snippets (`/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/user_service_notifications.go:318-391`).

### 4. Exact fields extracted/derived

From `internal/markdown/markdown.go` `ExtractAll` (persisted into `MemoPayload`):
- `Title` — extracted from the first H1 heading if it's the first block-level element (lines 384-388, helper `extractHeadingText`).
- `HasLink` — true if any markdown link node present (line 393-394).
- `HasCode` — true if any code block/fenced code block/code span present (lines 396-397).
- `HasTaskList` — true if any task checkbox present (lines 399-400).
- `HasIncompleteTasks` — true if any unchecked task checkbox present (lines 401-404).
- `Tags` — `#tag` nodes collected and deduplicated case-preserving (line 377, 418, helper `uniquePreserveCase`).
- `Mentions` — `@username` mention nodes, lowercased and deduplicated (line 379-380, 419) — used for notification dispatch (`memo_mention_helpers.go`), not stored in `MemoPayload`.

Computed at read-time (not stored):
- `Snippet` — plain-text summary, markdown stripped, code blocks skipped, truncated to `maxLength` (default 64 chars) at a word boundary (`GenerateSnippet`, lines 264-346).

Not derived from content (user/request-set, for completeness): `Location` (lat/long/placeholder) is set from the request, not extracted from text (`memo_service.go:112`, `:483`).</result>
